note: Answers to in-city slug collisions that scripts/identity/audit.mjs refuses to guess at. The audit holds every member of a collision until a resolution here names which row keeps the slug and which are held. A resolution is a citation, not an opinion: it needs a basis and, where the answer comes from an operator, the source that states it. A stale entry is an error, not a no-op — the audit throws if a resolution names a slug that is not in the collision it claims to settle, or leaves a member of that collision unaccounted for.

WA/bellevue/hillaire-park.basis: The City of Bellevue publishes exactly one Hillaire Park. Its A-Z park index, which appears in the navigation of every Bellevue park page, carries the name once, and the park's own page gives 15803 NE 6th St, Bellevue, WA 98008 — an address the Census geocoder matched to Bellevue city, King County. The kept row carries that address. The held row's street_address is "East Lake Hills", a neighbourhood rather than an address, with no house number to resolve, and its coordinates sit 4.7 km west of the park the City documents. It is a second record of the same park with a worse location, not a second park: the City's inventory has nowhere to put it. It stays quarantined and status=pending, so nothing is published from it and nothing is lost from data.csv.

WI/madison/tenney-park.basis: The City of Madison publishes one Tenney Park. Its pickleball courts list gives the address as 1414 E. Johnson St., which is the kept row's address and the one the Census geocoder matched to Madison city, Dane County. The held row carries 402 N Thornton Ave, 301 metres away on the far side of the same 38-acre park, and no City record names a second Tenney Park there. Two records of one park, distinguished only by which edge of it somebody stood on. The held row stays quarantined and status=pending; nothing is published from it and nothing is lost from data.csv.
